8.content:
Experian Credit Report

Credit Account

If you do not recognise an account, it could be one of the following reasons.

Some lenders use other names
This happens when companies offer credit for different stores or brands. The one that finances the agreement will give us this information, not the one where you opened the account.

For example, Shop Direct offers branded cards for many clothes and lifestyle brands including Littlewoods, Very and The Very Group. 
The Financial Conduct Authority also have a list of other trading names companies use. 

Defaulted accounts can be sold
This means you may not recognise the account because it was sold to a different company in order to recover the money owed. This happens when companies sell debts to other companies. Usually, it's because they can stop chasing outstanding payments and leave that to the debt collector. 

This may seem daunting but try not to worry. Speak to the company as soon as possible as they can help you arrange a payment plan.
Help if you're worried about debt

A financial connection is someone you're linked to through joint finances or accounts.

If you no longer share finances with someone, you can ask us to remove them from your credit report. You'll also need to ask Equifax and TransUnion too.

If you still share a mortgage, we may be able to remove someone if you've been living apart for more than six months. But you'll need to close all other shared finances, such as joint bank accounts.

17.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

Search details

#selected_creditsearches# 

What is a hard search?

When you apply for credit, the company will perform a hard check of your credit report to assess your suitability. Utility providers and mobile phone companies may also complete hard checks when you apply for their services.

A hard credit check involves a complete search of your credit report. These checks are recorded on your report, making them visible to any company that searches it.

What does this mean for me?

Having too many hard credit checks in a short period can affect your credit score for six months, potentially reducing your chances of getting approved for credit in the future.

Related questions

How long do searches stay on my Experian Credit Report?
Why is a past search still showing on my credit report?

Experian Credit Report

Search

If you don't see the search listed, then it's likely to be a soft search.

Soft searches don't appear on your credit report, don't affect your credit score, and don't impact any applications you make. Companies need your permission to check your credit report and they might check it more than once to manage your account.

A common type of soft search is for insurance quotes, especially when your policy is up for renewal or if you’ve been looking for quotes on comparison websites. When you complete an insurance quote online, the terms and conditions often include a clause allowing a renewal search to be made when the policy is due to expire.

49.content:
Experian Credit Report

I want to explain something on my report 

If there’s anything on your credit report that you think is misleading or needs explaining, you can ask for a Notice of Correction to be included. This is a short statement which you can use to add further information to a record in your Experian Credit Report.

For example, you could use it to explain why you fell behind with the repayments on a particular loan or credit agreement. Any lender checking your Experian Credit Report will see your statement and should take it into account when assessing your creditworthiness.

Related questions

50.content:
Experian Credit Report

I want to explain something on my report 

When adding a notice of correction, you must make sure it:

  • Includes details about which entry on your Experian Credit Report you want to add the notice of correction to, including the name of the company your account is with and the date of the record you want to explain (such as the date of your missed credit card payment).
  • Is no longer than 200 words and includes only factual information relevant only to that specific entry. In other words don't reference or blame another company or person for the problem you're explaining.
  • Follows this format adding your own words in the square brackets:
    [[COPY-AREA]] I, Mr/Mrs/Ms [name here], would like to explain the circumstances that led to the late payments/defaults recorded against the account [account name] started on [DD/MM/YYYY]. I [became unemployed] and my income was reduced to [£income]. Unfortunately, I was unable to keep the original payment contract. I ask all lenders searching my credit report to take this into account.[[/COPY-AREA]] Copy example statement

To add your notice of correction, please fill out the below form. 

Alternatively, you can post it to us at the below address:

96.content:
Experian Credit Report

My report and the new Experian Credit Score

Your Experian Credit Score just got smarter
We’ve changed the way your score is calculated and how it looks. It now includes more information to better reflect how lending works today. We’ve expanded the score range from 0 to 1250 to give you a more accurate view of how you’re doing. Plus, there are now more ways to improve your score - from trimming your overdraft to avoiding cash withdrawals on credit cards.

Will the new score impact what's in my credit report?
No. This will not impact the information in your report, or your eligibility for credit. Your new score simply gives you a clearer picture of how lenders now assess your credit report. It won’t change the information lenders are seeing when they look at your report.

111.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

This is a soft search

Search details
#selected_softCreditSearches#

What does this mean?

Soft searches don't appear on your credit report, don't affect your credit score, and don't impact any applications you make. Companies need your permission to check your credit report and they might check it more than once to manage your account.

A common type of soft search is for insurance quotes, especially when your policy is up for renewal or if you’ve been looking for quotes on comparison websites. When you complete an insurance quote online, the terms and conditions often include a clause allowing a renewal search to be made when the policy is due to expire.

112.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

This is an insurance quotation search

Search details
#selected_softCreditSearches#

What does this mean?

Insurance quotes are a common type of soft search, especially when your policy is up for renewal or if you’ve been looking for quotes on comparison websites. When you complete an insurance quote online, the terms and conditions often include a clause allowing a renewal search to be made when the policy is due to expire.

The great news is that as they are soft searches, they don't appear on your credit report, don't affect your credit score, and don't impact any applications you make.

Insurance quotation searches are kept on your Experian Credit Report for only 3 months from the date the search was carried out.

113.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

This is an identification check

Search details

#selected_softCreditSearches#

What does this mean?

Companies may carry out these searches to confirm your identity, often as part of their account management processes, periodic Know Your Customer checks, or when you’re using a service linked to an existing account.

The great news is that because these are soft searches, they don’t appear to other companies, won’t affect your credit score, and won’t impact any applications you make.

If you’re unsure why this search was carried out, you can contact the company directly for more information.

If you’d like to learn more, take a look at our article about searches on your credit report.

What does this mean?

These searches are recorded when you ask for a quote but haven’t applied for a product yet.

The great news is that because these are soft searches, they don’t appear to other companies, won’t affect your credit score, and won’t impact any applications you make.

We’ve got a great guide about credit searches if you want to learn more about this.

115.page_title: Customer selected "not listed" on search dropdowns
115.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

The search isn't showing on your Experian Credit Report

Here are some reasons why you might not see the search:
  • The company may have used a different credit reference agency, not Experian.
  • The search may have been done over 12 months ago and has now been removed from your report.
  • Your report may be missing information if you didn’t provide all your addresses from the past 6 years, or if you haven’t updated your address after moving. Your report only shows information linked to the addresses you’ve given us.

This is a credit report search

#selected_softCreditSearches#

What does this mean?

The Experian searches you’ve seen on your report are only there to let you know when you’ve applied for your credit report. They show for you so you can see each time you’ve checked a new report.

Don’t worry – companies can’t see these types of searches and they won’t impact your Experian Credit Score.

For more information take a look at our article on searches on your report.

118.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

This is an Experian identification check

Search details
#selected_softCreditSearches#

What does this mean?

The Experian search you can see on your report is created when you apply to access your credit report. This check helps confirm your identity and keep your information secure.

You may notice two searches from us:
  • an identity check, and
  • a credit report search

Don’t worry — these searches are only visible to you, cannot be seen by other companies and won’t affect your Experian Credit Score.

For more information take a look at our article on searches on your report.

119.content:
Experian Credit Report

Search

This search is recorded by LexisNexis

Search details

#selected_softCreditSearches# 

What does this mean?

You may not recognise LexisNexis, but they work with many banks, insurers and other financial companies. They help businesses confirm people’s identities, meet legal requirements and protect against fraud.

For example, LexisNexis may help verify your identity when you transfer money overseas, update your pension or apply for insurance.

These checks are only visible to you and will not affect your credit score or credit report.

120.content:
Experian Credit Report

A financial connection

What is a financial connection?

A financial connection is someone you're linked to through joint finances or accounts.

How can I remove a financial connection?

If you no longer share finances with someone, you can ask us to remove them from your credit report. You'll also need to ask Equifax and TransUnion too.

If you still share a mortgage, we may still be able to remove them. But you'll need to close all other shared finances, such as joint bank accounts.
